analysis: Examined units are CI test scripts for the threat-review tooling, not provider, coordinator or native-runtime code. .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py head adds imports (Scanner, ThreatContext at lines 12, 15) and tests: workload call policy admits planned stages and blocks unplanned calls (lines 301-316); emergency ceiling stops unadmitted stages (318-331); invalid policies/ceiling fail closed (333-340); a large hierarchical scan test (396-440); and final incomplete results requiring human review (482-499). .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py head lines 949-982 add tests: a manual rerun hands off without paid work, and its report does not clear; runtime bounds of 60-3000s; workload-ceiling handoff diagnostics. These tests assert fail-closed merge-gate behavior (clean() false on incomplete or stale results; a rerun requires the result of the current attempt). They do not touch threat-model assets (A-001..A-017) or boundaries TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-009/TB-010/TB-011. No product attack surface changed. The test files themselves contain only synthetic ARNs and tokens and no secrets. The implementation files (threat_review/bedrock.py plan_calls, threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds, the rerun handling in budget_runner) are not in this batch. Integration should confirm that these files enforce the asserted fail-closed limits, especially that the workload ceiling cannot exceed the 100 cap and that a rerun cannot reuse a prior attempt's clearance. This affects CI cost and merge-gate integrity, not provider security. No regression identified.
